reason: E1 directly supports the SCCP mechanism and strength-ductility improvement in tungsten RHEAs. E2 supports the general promise of RHEAs for high-temperature use. E3 suggests that compositional complexity may improve He irradiation tolerance, but does not address SCCPs or coherent precipitates. The key premise linking SCCPs specifically to improved radiation tolerance is not supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations in RHEAs.
SCCPs can increase strength without seriously compromising tensile ductility in tungsten RHEAs.
RHEAs are prospective materials for high-temperature applications.
Increasing compositional complexity in RHEAs may increase tolerance to He irradiation.
